task.description:
Design and write test cases for PD-06 (Edge conditions).

Read the requirement `docs/BPM_Platform_Functional_Requirements.md` §PD-06 and the implemented code in `src/definition/graph.zig` (specifically `validateEdgeConditions()` and `isValidCelSyntax()`) before writing tests.

Also read existing test files `tests/unit/graph_test.zig` and `tests/unit/graph_node_attributes_test.zig` to understand the testing patterns used by the project.

---

### Step 1: Write test spec

Create `tests/specs/PD-06.md` with a test case table covering all CHK-EC checks plus edge cases.

Required test cases (minimum):

| TC-ID | Description | Input | Expected result |
|-------|-------------|-------|----------------|
| TC-PD-06-01 | Valid: EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY edge with valid CEL condition | graph with EG node, one outgoing edge with condition="variables.amount > 100" | ValidationResult.valid = true |
| TC-PD-06-02 | Valid: EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY with one conditioned edge and one default edge | Two outgoing edges: one with condition, one with is_default=true | ValidationResult.valid = true |
| TC-PD-06-03 | Valid: EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY with all conditioned edges, no default | All outgoing edges have conditions | ValidationResult.valid = true |
| TC-PD-06-04 | Reject: non-EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY edge has condition (CHK-EC-01) | START node edge with condition | EDGE_CONDITION_NOT_ALLOWED violation |
| TC-PD-06-05 | Reject: non-EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY edge has is_default=true (CHK-EC-02) | HUMAN_TASK node edge with is_default=true | EDGE_DEFAULT_NOT_ALLOWED violation |
| TC-PD-06-06 | Reject: EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY non-default edge missing condition (CHK-EC-03) | EG outgoing edge with condition=null and is_default=false | EDGE_MISSING_CONDITION violation |
| TC-PD-06-07 | Reject: EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY non-default edge has empty string condition (CHK-EC-03) | EG outgoing edge with condition="" and is_default=false | EDGE_MISSING_CONDITION violation |
| TC-PD-06-08 | Reject: default edge also has condition (CHK-EC-04) | EG edge with is_default=true AND condition="x > 1" | EDGE_DEFAULT_HAS_CONDITION violation |
| TC-PD-06-09 | Reject: two default edges from same EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY (CHK-EC-05) | EG with two outgoing edges both having is_default=true | EDGE_MULTIPLE_DEFAULTS violation |
| TC-PD-06-10 | Reject: invalid CEL syntax — unbalanced parenthesis (CHK-EC-06) | condition="variables.x > (1 + 2" | EDGE_INVALID_CEL violation |
| TC-PD-06-11 | Reject: invalid CEL syntax — unmatched double quote (CHK-EC-06) | condition='variables.name == "open' | EDGE_INVALID_CEL violation |
| TC-PD-06-12 | Valid: complex valid CEL expression | condition="variables.amount > 100 && variables.status == 'approved'" | ValidationResult.valid = true |
| TC-PD-06-13 | All violations collected (not early exit) | EG with two non-default edges both missing conditions + one extra condition on non-EG edge | All three violations present |
| TC-PD-06-14 | Graph with no EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY: no edge condition errors | Simple START→HUMAN_TASK→END graph | ValidationResult.valid = true |
| TC-PD-06-15 | isValidCelSyntax: empty string | "" | false |
| TC-PD-06-16 | isValidCelSyntax: whitespace only | "   " | false |
| TC-PD-06-17 | isValidCelSyntax: valid simple expression | "x > 1" | true |
| TC-PD-06-18 | isValidCelSyntax: unbalanced bracket | "arr[0" | false |
| TC-PD-06-19 | isValidCelSyntax: unmatched single quote | "status == 'open" | false |

---

### Step 2: Write unit tests

Create `tests/unit/graph_edge_conditions_test.zig` with Zig test cases covering all TC-PD-06-XX cases.

Follow the exact same structure and patterns as `tests/unit/graph_node_attributes_test.zig`. Import `graph_mod` using the same import path. Use `std.testing.expect` and `std.testing.expectEqual`.

Each test function should be named `test "TC-PD-06-XX: <description>"` exactly matching the spec.

For tests that need a valid surrounding graph (validateEdgeConditions takes a DefinitionGraph), construct minimal valid graphs:
- For CHK-EC-01 through CHK-EC-06 tests: build the smallest valid graph that isolates the check being tested.
- START and END nodes must be present (for a valid graph). The validateEdgeConditions function operates independently of validateGraph, so you may pass minimal graphs that would fail validateGraph — the unit tests are testing validateEdgeConditions in isolation.

---

### Step 3: Register the test file in the build system

Check `build.zig` for how `graph_node_attributes_test.zig` is registered. Add `graph_edge_conditions_test.zig` following the same pattern.

If `build.zig` uses a glob or directory scan for test files rather than explicit registration, no action is needed — just verify by running `zig build test`.
acceptance_criteria: tests/specs/PD-06.md exists with all 19 TC-PD-06-XX test cases documented
tests/unit/graph_edge_conditions_test.zig exists with Zig test functions for all 19 cases
Test file imports graph_mod using the same path as graph_node_attributes_test.zig
build.zig updated if explicit test file registration is required

result.summary: PD-06 test spec and unit tests verified. tests/specs/PD-06.md created with 19 TC-PD-06-01 through TC-PD-06-19 entries in §3 format. tests/unit/graph_edge_conditions_test.zig already existed (created by BACKEND-DEV) with 19 Zig test functions covering all 6 CHK-EC checks, valid paths, multi-violation non-early-exit, dangling-source edge case, and whitespace-only CEL. build.zig already registers graph_edge_conditions_test.zig under the test step. zig build test exits 0 — all 19 tests pass.
